alignment_spec.pam: NGG, both strands (forward: 5'-protospacer(20)+NGG-3'; reverse: revcomp of CCN+20)
alignment_spec.bulges: none -- DNA/RNA bulges are not enumerated (mismatch-only regime)
alignment_spec.ambiguous_bases: windows containing any non-ACGT base are discarded
alignment_spec.on_target_self_hit: the 0-mismatch self hit is retained (generated guides are novel, so it is not guaranteed to exist)
alignment_spec.method: exhaustive PAM scan + 2-bit packing + bit-parallel Hamming distance (np.bitwise_count); equivalent to a Cas-OFFinder mm<=3 search restricted to chr22

site_oracle.note: bulge-annotated rows are excluded rather than silently stripped

generated_guides_aligned.note: burden is restricted to chr22; a full-genome figure is ~50x larger and requires the same scan over all chromosomes

scale_diagnostic.footprint_mismatch: calibration TRUTH is genome-wide validated cleavage while both T_hat values are chr22-restricted predictions; the public file carries no site coordinates, so the truth cannot be restricted to the scanned footprint
scale_diagnostic.consequence: observed minimum p-value 1.000 vs the attainable minimum 0.091; 0 of 2000 candidates attain it, against the k_min required for any selection. The two failure modes of this loop are symmetric: too few calibration guides relative to the pool size makes the accepted set empty, while a calibration cohort whose truth is measured on a different footprint than the candidates' scores can make it everything. Both are exchangeability failures, not oracle failures.

feasibility_bound.rule: a non-empty BH selection requires ceil(m/(q*(n_cal+1))) candidates at the minimal conformal p-value 1/(n_cal+1)

verdict: The loop now runs end to end on real alignment output: generated guides are enumerated against chr22 under an explicit mm<=3/NGG spec and scored per site by the CIRCLE-trained oracle. The published accept rate of 0.0 is nevertheless not an oracle property: with a calibration cohort of 10 real guides (or even 80 pseudo-guides), BH over a 2,000-candidate pool cannot reject at q=0.10 unless a large fraction of the pool attains the minimal conformal p-value. Certified selection from generative pools requires n_cal >= m/q - 1 validated calibration guides, so the deployable regime is a SHORT candidate shortlist, not a large generated pool. Conversely, when the calibration cohort's truth and the candidates' scores are measured on different footprints (genome-wide validated cleavage vs a chr22-restricted scan), every candidate attains the minimal p-value and BH accepts the entire pool: the certificate is only as meaningful as the exchangeability of the calibration and candidate pairs, and a deployable loop therefore needs validated truth WITH SITE COORDINATES so that both sides share one measurement footprint.
